Image, PDF, Office, audio and video reacquire only on own/ancestor or unknown changes, publish the replacement and release the old native snapshot. Hidden and rebound reads are fenced; failed refresh preserves the shown snapshot and Retry reacquires from the provider. Native Arc ownership replaces TS URL revocation. Image admission consumes provider-authorized bounded snapshots off the UI thread; replacement, revocation and disposal cancel owned work, fence replies and evict stale decode assets. AVIF conversion has bounded input/output, deadlines and child-process cleanup; actual Retry and damaged-image decoding are exercised. Media surfaces grant one provider resource, use leased readers for HEAD and Range without whole-file copies, preserve registered MIME for extensionless inputs, and retire protocol clones and stale frame IPC on replacement, failure, revocation or disposal. Additional native decoder acceptance bounds source bytes and rejects excessive original raster expansion before decoding, including grayscale-to-RGBA and sixteen-bit pixels; all five enabled fallback codecs, invalid/oversized headers, premultiplied BGRA, downsampling and real macOS sips output are exercised. The 64 MiB raster admission and best-effort codec limits are not a process RSS ceiling or a claim that Chromium uses this native implementation.

contracts.acceptance: Real Documents coordinators, a controllable text storage provider and the actual DocumentEditor surfaces for every editable preset viewer: Markdown, plain text, Python, JSON, CSV, TSV, HTML (source and preview), whiteboard, Context Map and PuppyFlow; the completeness case asserts the fixture viewers equal the manifest's edit-capable viewers. Clean storage updates reach the view with exactly one reread and no write, and unrelated paths never reread. Dirty local text yields to storage without a conflict or writeback, and a later manual save writes once against the adopted revision (the native port has no TS persistence 'reason' field; the explicit save intent is the trigger). Destroying the whole host and recreating it shows the latest storage or saved text without saving again, and every view is asserted released. For web-page formats the GPUI matrix stands in for the page with its protocol messages and checks the boot document a (re)created page would show; real WKWebView probes over the production Wry IPC prove the page side: the shipped Context Map and PuppyFlow bundles apply resets, report edits tagged with the adopted generation, undo/redo, keep history while hidden and shown, refuse read-only edits and lose history only to a reset; the installed Excalidraw pack replaces scenes on reset and tags later drawings; the HTML preview loads the replaced document. Undo/redo after a view is destroyed: native text and CSV models belong to the open document instance (DocumentModels), the next view of the same text continues them, and closing, another document, an unseen storage update and an open IME composition each isolate them; WB-01 hibernation carries them. A web page's model history cannot be detached, so instead a page that edited is never destroyed while its document is open: it is pinned against WebView eviction and its slot against hibernation until a reset clears the history (platform substitution for the product's model-owner remount). Edits a structured page posted before a reset can no longer overwrite the new text, an evicted whiteboard returns with the current text and generation, and a closed HTML surface releases its pages and source view. One watcher batch updates two panes with one own-path reread each; an obsolete read (serialized per path natively) never reaches the view; a failed refresh keeps the stable text and recovers on retry; a pathless notification rereads.

contracts.acceptance: A cancelled window close thaws every retained copy in place: no editor is shown again (only Thaw reaches the hosts), observers stay live, and a later disk change still reaches the copy (the native runtime owners are the working copy's watch and I/O owners, not React task contexts). A document's history keeps its newest 200 steps and a pending redo when its view is destroyed and the next view of the same text attaches. For Markdown, plain text and Python, a saved edit survives destroying the whole host; reattaching writes nothing, and undo/redo on the new view each autosave once (alpha, then the edit). When storage changes a document whose view is gone, the next view shows the storage text, writes nothing more and has nothing to undo. Decided difference (ADR-013, DP-03): an external adoption while the view is alive is an undoable sealed step instead of a fresh history, so overwritten input can be recovered; the TS fresh-history behaviour holds only when no view saw the change.

contracts.acceptance: Local folders persist through the real document session and the local provider's conditional writes. A Markdown keyboard edit autosaves once to the real file after the typing pause, as does an HTML edit made in the source view chosen from the pane menu (source edit appended after the original bytes). In a CSV, a cell edit, an added field, an added record and a 2x2 size-picker growth each autosave the exact serialized table, and the grid shows 4 records of 5 fields. A newer revision typed while the first write is still in flight is captured and drained before close, and reopening reads it. A local edit whose save keeps failing (the folder refuses writes) keeps its text, dirty state and failure while the person opens another file and comes back; the file on disk is untouched. A Terminal or Agent change to an open Markdown file is adopted with one reread and no write, and unrelated paths do not reread. The native port has no TS expectedVersion field: the local provider's conditional write against the read revision is the counterpart, and its success is the observable.

The native kernel sends model requests only to the connection's own chat-completions path, from canonical endpoints; a session is bound to one connection and its text-and-tool models, keys are write-only and never reach a shell the model can call. Verification runs the real tool round trip against a local HTTP service and fails a model that answers without calling the check tool. A write waits for approval and reports its change, a saved session reopens with its history without a connection, and the approval, resume, stop and binding run over real HTTP. Rust's kernel is native, so there is no SDK worker, private pipe or fetch interceptor to bound.

contracts.acceptance: A first publication runs through the real git CLI against a smart-HTTP Cloud Git with a scripted Cloud API, crashing at each durable point and resuming in a fresh coordinator. An unborn branch is refused before anything is created; a feature branch is created once and lands on Cloud main with the credential out of the journal and every stage in order; a crash after the remote is added, the Project or the credential is created, or the push lands resumes without another Project; lost Project, credential and discard responses are replayed with the same Idempotency-Key, body and secret; every API request names repository contract 2. A pending operation meeting another remote, a repointed remote and an edited journal fail closed: the journaled remote is re-validated before any secret is read or network Git runs (Rust now does this; where TS continues to the journaled URL after its check, Rust refuses on its later check, and nothing reaches the other place). The helper is pinned against a local config race, only the committed tree is sent, an attempt keeps its commit after HEAD moves, Push latest starts a new attempt, and a Cloud main that wins the absent race is never overwritten. Unresolved sends are retried with their commit; restarts while uploading or confirming offer Retry; an old upload landing first is not a failure; a second failure keeps the unresolved commit; identical publications at once share one run (Rust now singleflights them) and create one Project. Cleanup finishes after a failure and checkout changes, replays a lost discard, finishes after a crash that removed the remote, lets Cloud prove emptiness, reconciles Cloud main when Cloud refuses (Rust now does), and a definitive refusal keeps sending available across restarts. A deleted source branch can be replaced, an unavailable Project offers only Finish cleanup, version-1 journals migrate (and are written back on first read, as Rust now does) and resume by Cloud main. Every repository shape but Git LFS is accepted under the pinned contract; linked worktrees share the repository owner.

contracts.acceptance: Cloud Git credentials are scoped to the canonical URL. The managed helper resets only that URL's chain and is pinned on every command, and the secret goes to it on standard input, never argv. Only an allowlisted helper is chosen; on macOS that is the keychain, so failing closed with none is the Linux path. Shell and path helpers never receive the secret. Abandon and Detach restore the values that were there before, and an oversized snapshot is refused before the config changes (Rust now bounds snapshots: 64 values of 4 KiB each, 64 KiB encoded). A helper that cannot read the credential back fails closed and restores the config, with no secret in the error (Rust's message does not quote the helper's stderr). A concurrent local change to the managed scope is detected (Rust now asserts the scope after configuring the remote, after a push and before finalizing). A restore cut short resumes, and every config-write crash point of install and restore recovers. The system keychain is never written in tests: a private store file stands in.

contracts.acceptance: An explicit opening of a Cloud workspace hands its verified root over once. A running workspace is checked and its files read with one status and one listing request; a prepared opening is a one-use receipt the next opening does not reuse, and one that expired, whose generation moved, or whose sign-in ended is refused before its root is shown. Openings of the same target join one pending opening and share its progress; progress names the server's phase, starts with checking, moves to files for a running workspace, and starts over on retry. A sleeping workspace is woken with exactly one request and then long-polled (wait_seconds=20); a server that ignores the long poll is asked at most once a second while a ready answer is used at once. knownDifferences.reason: TS runs each database engine in a supervised UtilityProcess: quota is released only after the host exit is confirmed, probe and query timeouts and memory are enforced independently of an unresponsive host, and file locks are released after a host crash. Cancelling while an open is pending therefore does not wait for a host exit, and there is no close handle kept for retry after an unconfirmed exit.

knownDifferences.reason: These assert the declarations of particular CSS rules (a selector's shadow, gap, grid columns, weight, colour, scrollbar pseudo-elements, resize-lane widths) by reading the TS stylesheets as text. The native frontend has no stylesheet or cascade to read: each GPUI component sets its geometry and paint directly, with values ported from the cited TS rule, and visual parity is reviewed by capturing both products and comparing the captures (tools/capture-*.py, tools/compare.py, tools/compare-native-geometry.py) rather than by text assertions. Rules that carry product meaning beyond one selector have native tests in their rows: the elevation scale, the opaque selection paint, the typography role tables and the file-icon slot.

knownDifferences.reason: TS v0.4.4 retired the Cloud Hub: its router, sidebar, main view and Share wizard are deleted (cloudNavigationInformationArchitecture asserts it) and Cloud destinations such as Access, Team and Billing open on the Web. The Overview, Access and Connections, Automation (with its Synchronize API client), project Settings, Billing and Organization page components, their route table, domain helpers and stylesheets remain in the repository, but no desktop view mounts them (AutomationRouteSection, OverviewSection, CloudProjectSettingsSection and CloudOrganizationBillingPage are imported by nothing, and only the Automation UI calls the Synchronize functions), so these cases describe pages and logic a person cannot reach in the product. The native frontend never had the Hub, and its Cloud pieces (publication, Cloud projects, the Cloud Computer, sharing and plans) have their own rows.

knownDifferences.reason: These call the Electron main process's local API module directly (electron/local-api: its file-format and path helpers and its Git source-control presentation model), which shapes the data the TS renderer receives over IPC. The native app has no such module or process boundary: formats resolve through the shared format registry, workspace paths are typed provider-relative paths that refuse any parent, root or absolute component, and the Changes sidebar reads the Git snapshot directly. The product behaviour behind these helpers is mapped in the format-routing, workspace-file-operation and Git rows.

They cover the project backup provider list, the remote update notice, the file-open request coordinator and its content cache, a standalone Terminal session host, the old Terminal workbench header, and the Cloud remote-name and reviewed Git-state guards of workspaceGitRemote.ts (exported functions nothing calls). knownDifferences.reason: TS resolves Markdown assets through an AssetBroker that hands features capability URLs (including provider-resolved loopback URLs) under host leases it revokes, validates sinks and purposes, and runs trusted local HTML in revocable execution sessions. The native editor reads asset bytes itself through the workspace or provider after the same policy (no URLs, leases or capability purposes), and never executes HTML in Markdown (executable HTML is removed from the native flow), so its features are given no HTML trust mode. The rest of that embed runtime is likewise TS's own: embedded edit sessions that commit a draft against a base revision (native widget commands re-derive their edit from the current source, so no draft can go stale), widget sessions disposed by DOM node, web embeds bound to a capability principal and revision with single-flight native view creation (a native embed is keyed by its view, block and URL, and a loading one takes no second click), principal-scoped render deduplication (the native render service shares one job per drawing), and explicit grants for local active HTML. No authored source URL ever reaches a live browser sink either, because the native surface hands images bytes, not URLs. A media block therefore needs no broker at plan time (natively it renders and reads its bytes when shown), and remote badges load through the pinned HTTPS client rather than browser image sinks with referrer, CORS and lazy-loading attributes.

knownDifferences.reason: TS hands viewers blob or capability URLs from a reference-counted pool (shared acquisitions, replacement published before the old URL is revoked, failed revocations retried, sibling cancellation isolated, admission closed during window retirement), retires native host surfaces through leases, and re-prepares a document when a tracked resource or directory dependency changes. The native editor decodes resources into one bounded cache keyed by content stamp with generation-guarded settles, holds native surfaces by ownership, and re-resolves references when the workspace changes, so there are no URLs to revoke, leases to retire or dependency index to keep.

native editor host ownership > retains a failed native release for retry and leaves unrelated resources alive
editor resource ownership > blocks late allocations during window retirement and reopens admission after cancellation
editor resource ownership > shares one acquisition and releases only after the final consumer
editor resource ownership > publishes replacement URLs to every remaining subscriber before revoking the old URL
editor resource ownership > keeps failed capability revocation pending until a retry really succeeds
editor resource ownership > does not let one cancelled acquisition cancel a sibling consumer
editor dependency preparation > ignores matching entries already consumed from an accumulated notification
editor dependency preparation > keeps accepted dependencies while preparing and rejects a stale replacement

knownDifferences.reason: TS keys a document by a string resource path, so it canonicalizes legacy provider paths (backslashes, `./`, doubled slashes) and keeps `puppyone-local://` Workspace Resource URIs whole. Native documents are keyed by their storage and a relative path inside an admitted root, so there is no string form to canonicalize.

knownDifferences.reason: TS serves immutable preview snapshots through a main-process URL service: unguessable URLs, GET and HEAD only, forged paths and fragments refused, a UTF-8 budget per snapshot, 128 retained leases per owner and revocation only by the owning sender. A native HTML preview's web view is handed its page by the viewer that owns it, under the same opaque sandbox (scripts and forms, no same origin or top navigation; html_preview::tests::page_scripts_run_inside_the_sandbox_boundaries), so there are no URLs to forge, revoke or bound.

provider-neutral immutable preview documents > permits page interaction in an opaque sandbox and restricts revocation to the owning sender
provider-neutral immutable preview documents > rejects forged paths, methods and unbounded UTF-8 allocations
provider-neutral immutable preview documents > bounds retained leases and releases capacity on owner close

knownDifferences.reason: TS allocates parse workers per owner through a scheduler: one allocation per owner at a time, cancelled queued work never allocated, asynchronous allocations accounted until their exit is confirmed, failed exits retried on retirement, oversized input refused before allocating and queue waits bounded. Native document work runs on one bounded thread pool with per-request generations (documents::tests::dp41_dp42_bounded_executor_thread_ceiling_and_exact_deadline_scheduling) and oversized sources are refused before reading, so there are no worker allocations to account for or exit.

editor task lifecycle > keeps an asynchronously created allocation accounted until its actual exit
editor task lifecycle > keeps failed exits visible and allows a retirement retry
editor task lifecycle > rejects oversized input before allocating and bounds waiting time

knownDifferences.reason: TS sessions also run in a manual save mode that the desktop never uses (every desktop host passes saveMode="auto"; manual is the shared library default and performance harnesses'), and they publish whether a window holds unsaved edits through an exported subscription nothing in the product reads. The native desktop autosaves every document and has neither.

knownDifferences.reason: TS coordinates a window close across the Electron main process and its renderer: it ignores a flush acknowledgement forged by another renderer and must not touch a destroyed BrowserWindow that closes before it is ready. The product never configures its close-choice question (resolveCloseChoice defaults to save), so the ask / don't-save / cancel / ask-again / asking-failed paths are unreachable. The native close drains documents in process and asks only when a document could not be saved.

knownDifferences.reason: TS's renderer persists a document through an IPC adapter that must forward the session's base version to the authorized conditional write and carry the structured conflict, not-found, permission-denied and io outcomes back across the process boundary. Native sessions call the workspace provider in process with typed results (editor::document_session tests cover conditional writes and each outcome).

knownDifferences.reason: TS mounts a bounded window of DOM rows and columns (prefix geometry for variable widths, a mounted-item cap, directional and velocity-predicted overscan) so fast scrolling stays inside rendered rows. The native grid paints exactly the rows and columns that intersect the viewport on every frame, so there are no mounted items, caps or overscan to predict; large-table cost is covered by the CSV view tests (large_csv_parses_in_background_while_showing_readonly_preview_and_respects_replace_text) and the csv_table_cost bench.

knownDifferences.reason: TS hosts declare their navigation capabilities, so a host without external opening reports external links unavailable, and a host may cancel a workspace open or return no outcome that the port must preserve. Every native editor host opens external links through the app and requests workspace opens as fire-and-forget events, so there is no missing capability or returned outcome.

knownDifferences.reason: Natively HTML renders only as its own block. Inline HTML runs stay visible source: images, linked images and theme pictures inside a paragraph, list item, task, heading, quote or table cell (README badge and download-card lines), passive elements such as font, big, dfn, nobr, meter or an inline center, Markdown inside an inline run, an HTML block on the same line as a list or quote marker, empty elements that the product hides, and inline audio. With no runs there is also no run reveal on caret entry, fold on caret exit, selection spanning a run, nested blocked element reduction inside a run or isolated table-cell run preview.
